sections.h2: Kansas laws that govern landlords and tenants
sections.html:
Most residential rentals in Kansas fall under the Kansas Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, K.S.A. 58-2540 through 58-2573. Mobile home parks have their own act, and rentals of non-residential property are covered by K.S.A. 58-2501 through 58-2533.

K.S.A. 58-2573 carves out one group. The residential act does not protect a person who enters and stays in a dwelling without a rental agreement and without the landlord's knowledge, knowing they have no right to be there, after the landlord has personally told them to leave. A tenant under a rental agreement, written or not, is on the protected side of that line.

Many owners are surprised that a missing lease does not leave a gap. The statute fills it. If you inherit a rental with no lease on file and plan to sell, you are still bound by the act's notice, deposit and repair rules.

Common Kansas tenant rules and the amounts or time limits that go with them
TopicKansas rule
Security deposit, unfurnishedUp to one month's rent
Security deposit, furnishedUp to 1.5 months' rent
Pet depositUp to half a month's rent extra
Deposit return14 days after deductions are set, 30 days at most
Wrongful withholdingDamages of 1.5 times the amount withheld
Month-to-month ending30 days, on a rent-paying date
Week-to-week ending7 days
Landlord entryReasonable hours, reasonable notice

The deposit rules sit in K.S.A. 58-2550, the ending of tenancies in K.S.A. 58-2570 and entry in K.S.A. 58-2557. A federal rule also bars an extra deposit for a certified service or assistance animal.

sections.h2: What the landlord owes during the tenancy
sections.html:
A Kansas landlord must keep the rental fit to live in, and the tenant must keep paying rent regardless. The two duties are separate, so a tenant who holds back rent over repair problems can still be taken to court for nonpayment.

Under K.S.A. 58-2553, the landlord has to follow building and housing codes that affect health and safety. The landlord must also keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating and air-conditioning equipment that the landlord supplies in good working order, and must supply running water, reasonable hot water and heat.

When repairs are ignored, a tenant has two options:

  • Give written notice of at least 30 days ending on a rent-paying date. The landlord then has 14 days to begin repairs, or the lease ends on the date named.
  • Sue to force repairs and recover damages, including rent paid for a place that was not livable.

Tenants are advised to call the local housing or code office before choosing either route. A tenant may also make repairs under a separate written agreement with the landlord, and the cost can then come off the next rent payment, though work that building codes require should be done by the landlord.

If you are selling and you know a rental has open repair issues, expect those complaints to follow the property into the sale.

A landlord may enter at reasonable hours after reasonable notice to inspect, make repairs or show the unit to purchasers. K.S.A. 58-2557 sets no fixed number of hours, though 24 hours is common practice. Entry without consent is allowed in an extreme hazard.

For a seller, showings are the most frequent reason to come through the door. Written notice with a proposed time leaves a clear record of what was asked.

The statute also bars retaliation. Under K.S.A. 58-2572, a landlord may not raise rent or reduce services because the tenant complained to a code agency or to the landlord, or joined a tenants' union, and the tenant has a defense in a possession action. A sale-driven eviction that follows soon after a repair complaint can invite that defense.

sections.h2: When the landlord sells the house
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel the tenancy by itself, but it shifts who answers for what. K.S.A. 58-2554 relieves a landlord who conveys the premises in a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser of liability under the rental agreement and the act for events after written notice of the conveyance goes to the tenant. The former landlord stays liable for any deposit amount the tenant is entitled to.

The statute opens with the words "unless otherwise agreed," so the sale contract can split the deposit duty differently between buyer and seller. Ask the closing agent to state in the file who holds the deposit.

Owners preparing to sell a rental usually do the following:

  • Pull the lease, the move-in inspection list and the deposit record.
  • Send the tenant the written notice of the conveyance, and keep a dated copy.
  • Check whether any repair requests are outstanding.
  • Decide whether the buyer is taking the house with the tenant or vacant.

We buy houses as-is and can work with an occupied rental. Tell us what the lease says and what condition the house is in, and we will explain what a sale could look like.

A lease ends by its own terms, by proper notice, or through eviction. A landlord usually must give at least 30 days' notice that it will not renew, and many leases ask the tenant for more, sometimes 60 days.

A tenancy does not always end when the lease term does. If the landlord takes the next month's rent, a month-to-month tenancy often follows. If the landlord does not take it, the landlord can serve a three-day notice to leave. A tenant who moves out without telling the landlord may owe another month.

Deposits come with their own mechanics. The tenant has to move out entirely, tell the landlord, return the keys and make a written demand. A landlord who keeps part of the deposit should send an itemized list within 30 days of move-out. A tenant generally cannot use the deposit as last month's rent unless the landlord agrees.

sections.h2: Special situations that change the rules
sections.html:
Three situations come up often enough that sellers should know them.

  • Military orders: A service member with permanent change of station orders, a deployment order or a call to support an operation lasting at least 90 days can end a lease. The tenancy ends 30 days after the day rent is next due, or with 15 days' notice on a month-to-month tenancy.
  • Natural disaster: If fire, flood or tornado makes the home unlivable, the tenant does not have to stay and can end the lease with written notice.
  • Disability and fair housing: The federal Fair Housing Act bars discrimination in renting and selling housing on the basis of race, gender, religion, familial status, disability or ethnicity, and landlords must allow reasonable accommodations. A landlord may still consider criminal history, credit and financial stability.

If you are selling, fair housing rules apply to how you treat the tenant and any buyer.

Rent paid by mail counts as paid when it is properly sent, which is why tenants should keep dated proof.

sections.h2: Before you sell a tenant-occupied house
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps a rental sale from stalling. Gather the lease or a note of the oral terms, the rent ledger, the deposit amount and where it is held, and any written repair requests. Decide early whether the buyer will take the tenant or needs the house empty, since that choice drives which notice you send and when.

If the buyer wants a vacant house and the tenancy is month-to-month, the 30-day notice on a rent-paying date sets the earliest move-out. If a fixed term is still running, the lease controls unless the tenant agrees to leave sooner. Put any early move-out in writing, with the date and the deposit handling spelled out.

faqs.q: How much can a Kansas landlord charge for a security deposit?
faqs.a: Up to one month's rent for an unfurnished unit and 1.5 months for a furnished one, plus up to half a month's rent more if pets are allowed, under K.S.A. 58-2550.

faqs.q: How long does a Kansas landlord have to return a deposit?
faqs.a: 14 days after determining deductions, and no more than 30 days after the tenancy ends, possession is delivered and the tenant demands it. Wrongful withholding carries damages of 1.5 times the amount withheld.

faqs.q: What happens to the tenant if the landlord sells the house?
faqs.a: The tenancy continues. The landlord is relieved of later liability once written notice of the sale goes to the tenant, but still owes any deposit the tenant is entitled to.

faqs.q: Can a Kansas landlord show a rental to buyers?
faqs.a: Yes, at reasonable hours and after reasonable notice under K.S.A. 58-2557. Many landlords give 24 hours.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Kansas?
faqs.a: Written notice of at least 30 days, ending on a rent-paying date, from either side. Week-to-week tenancies need 7 days.
